hooks.prompt:
Nothing from this finished turn needs to be written to the team's long-term memory.

That sentence is the condition. Test it, and mind its direction: it is SATISFIED — {"ok": true} — when there is nothing to record, which is the common case and the right answer whenever you are unsure. It is UNSATISFIED — {"ok": false} — only when something clearly does need recording. Stating the condition negatively is deliberate: satisfied and "let the turn end" have to point the same way, or a correct finding gets written into a reason attached to the verdict that discards it.

Judge the whole turn from the conversation above. The block below is the raw hook payload, not the evidence: read exactly one field from it, `stop_hook_active`, and ignore the rest. Its `last_assistant_message` is a verbatim copy of the final message already in the conversation above — score the turn, not its closing summary.

Hook payload: $ARGUMENTS

Worth recording means exactly one of two things, because they are the only two writable without a human's say-so:
- an **Insight** — a non-obvious constraint, mechanism or understanding a future reader could not recover from the code or the commit log;
- an **Incident** — something broke, and what happened.

Both also have to be durable for the team. A mechanism discovered in throwaway scaffolding — a sandbox, a scratch script, a test harness built for this session — is not, however real the finding.

The condition therefore stays satisfied for everything else. That includes a decision and its rationale, a corrective lesson, and an agreement about how the team works: all worth keeping, none yours to ask for, because the capture skill holds them behind an explicit signal from the user that a hook cannot give. It also includes routine edits, answering a question, reading or searching code, formatting, work still in progress, and anything already recorded earlier in this turn. Judge the substance of the work, not the language it is written in.

Ask at most once per turn. The hook payload carries `stop_hook_active`: when it is true you have already asked during this turn and the note has been delivered, so the condition is satisfied — respond {"ok": true} regardless of what else the transcript shows. Answering otherwise re-enters the same turn and loops it.

Respond with exactly {"ok": true} and no other field when the condition holds. Omit `reason` there: it is discarded unread, and a reason worth writing means you meant {"ok": false} instead.

Otherwise respond {"ok": false, "reason": "..."}. The reason is fed back to Claude as its next instruction, so write it as one imperative sentence addressed to Claude: say whether it is an Insight or an Incident, name the subject, and tell it to run the `gutt-claude-code-plugin:memory-capture` skill. Name only those two types. Naming a Lesson, Decision or WorkingAgreement asks that skill to write something its own gate refuses, and withholding the type is no better — it leaves the classifier to guess, and a guess landing on Insight has written a gated class under the wrong label. Do not restate this response format inside the reason: a reason that quotes the JSON gets echoed back to the user as the assistant's answer.
